evidence_rules: Record IDs identify figure-specific observations, not author-assigned unique batch IDs. No universal cross-figure identity or exact synthesis-time mapping is provided.
Reported diameters mean major axis. Angstrom-to-nanometre conversions do not add measurement precision.
Equal-size TEM, optical and diffraction samples must not automatically be joined as the same specimen, or declared different specimens.
No curves have been digitized; no exact peak positions are inferred from graphs.
An ideal wurtzite rendering is illustrative. Actual particles show stacking faults; surface disorder is compatible with diffraction data and included in the authors' nonunique model.
TOP/TOPO is the synthesis cap; TEM preparation uses a pyridine dispersion. Do not infer exact ligand coverage on an imaged particle.
A figure-evidence locator is not a newly invented experimental batch.
All figure evidence remains ineligible for recipe-target training until an explicit sample-to-protocol mapping is established.
No exact spectral maxima, lattice spacings or coordinate pairs have been inferred from graph pixels.

tem.imaging: Bright field; aperture permits lattice images of (100), (002), (101) wurtzite planes.
tem.grid: 300-mesh copper, approximately 50 A amorphous carbon film
tem.preparation: Apply dilute pyridine dispersion; wait approximately 1 minute; wick away solution. Coverage controlled by concentration and contact time.
tem.sampling_note: Method discussion describes 30-50 particles measured on a single image. This is not an explicitly assigned N for each panel.

xrd.sample: Approximately 500 mg washed/dried powder pressed at 5000 psi into 0.5-inch pellets, without amorphous binder.
xrd.note: Only unambiguous acquisition fields carried here; do not silently modernize or correct printed instrument parameters.

accelerating_voltage.warning: Potential source error: unusually high for the stated instrument. Preserve as printed with this flag; no silent correction or SOP endorsement.

references: Marcus et al., J. Phys. Chem. 1991, 95, 1572
exafs.do_not: Do not label these as EXAFS measurements newly acquired in Murray 1993.
exafs.model_values_note: 2.63 A is the bulk CdSe bond length adopted with support from prior EXAFS. The 0.04 A^2 mean-square displacement is the constant thermal-disorder parameter used in these diffraction simulations, described as consistent with prior EXAFS; it is not a newly measured EXAFS result in this paper.

overall_structure.evidence_kind: author interpretation of TEM, XRD fits and cited constraints
overall_structure.finding: Predominantly wurtzite, slightly prolate particles with roughly one stacking fault per 6-7 planes along the elongated direction. Bulk-like mean bond length; surface disorder compatible with data.
overall_structure.limitation: Pure wurtzite/zincblende labels hide stacking disorder; surface geometry is not uniquely resolved.

additional_article_evidence.finding: During growth, absorption widths are used only as a crude indicator of size-distribution width. Typical linewidth is 50 nm FWHM; this is not the numerical linewidth of Figure 5.
Sharper features near selected sizes are proposed as possible kinetic or thermodynamic growth bottlenecks. These are not assigned reaction-time endpoints or a validated magic-size series.

Pyridine exchange enables polar/aromatic dispersion and causes a slight decrease in mean size and a small broadening. The proposed loss of Cd/Se-containing species is an author explanation; no numerical etching rate or ligand inventory is measured.

The authors model undercoordinated surface ions with radial shifts, conserving approximately bulk average bond length. The selected relaxation is explicitly nonunique and does not determine an actual surface structure.

quantities.property: modeled surface-cation inward displacement toward cylinder axis
model average-bond-length deviation bound from bulk
size above which modeled surface-disorder effect becomes imperceptible

additional_article_evidence.finding: Seven parameters: lattice constant, thermal disorder, crystallite size, aspect ratio, stacking-fault density, surface disorder and constant background. Bulk lattice and TEM size constrain two; four are fitted on one size then fixed across sizes; average fault density may vary. This is a working structural description, not a measured atomic-coordinate reconstruction.

For the approximately 12-angstrom species, authors say too few atoms exist to define a core crystal structure meaningfully as wurtzite versus zinc blende. Do not label the 1.2-nm case as an experimentally determined bulk polytype.

Finite size and faults broaden/convolve peaks; first-feature peak position alone is unreliable for lattice spacing or size. Authors recommend the (110) feature for crude Scherrer estimates rather than the merged (100)/(002)/(101) feature.
Samples in original growth solution retained strong, sharp emission after more than one year.
additional_article_evidence.sample_specificity: No figure-specific sample ID or detailed storage conditions.
additional_article_evidence.limitation: Not a quantified photostability test under continuous illumination.

Raman.evidence: No Raman spectrum, acquisition method or result in the 10-page main article. Introductory mention of vibrational confinement is context, not Raman data.
Raman.si_scope: Matching SI unverified; statement applies to inspected main article.

saed_conclusion.status: reported qualitatively in text; pattern not shown

source.section: Transmission Electron Microscopy, lower left column

saed_conclusion.finding: Selected-area electron diffraction is said to confirm predominantly wurtzite structure. Nonrandom orientation on carbon complicates line-shape interpretation; electron microdiffraction is proposed as a potential alternative and cited, not reported as a new figure.
saed_conclusion.display_recommendation: Show a clearly labeled text-only evidence card, not a generated SAED image or an XRD graph mislabeled SAED.
